newsitem.title: UK: Small UK Unionist party quits Belfast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Small UK Unionist party quits Belfast peace talks.

text.p: The U.K. Unionist party, one of the smaller parties favouring continued Northern Ireland union with Britain, said on Monday it was pulling out of peace talks in protest at the British government's stand on IRA guerrilla arms.
The decision was announced by party leader Robert McCartney in a statement to reporters at Stormont buildings, where the year-long talks are under way.
Another small unionist group committed to British rule of Northern Ireland, the Democratic Unionist Party, has hinted that it will also walk out of the talks.

The mainstream Ulster Unionist Party was holding talks with British Prime Minister Tony Blair in London to clarify its position on "arms decommissioning" in the wake of the IRA (Irish Republican Army) ceasefire announced at the weekend.

McCartney said: "The representatives of political terror have been strengthened at the expense of democratic politicians and the confidence of the pro-Union people that the government will protect their constitutional rights has never ever been lower."
